clue.text: Folk-songs for athletes?

definitions.meaning: a genre of melancholy folk music from the American South
at Oxford and Cambridge a sportsman who represents the university is awarded a Blue

explanation.surface: A question about which traditional songs suit sporting people.
explanation.walkthrough: A university Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge, so the plural doubles as the music.
explanation.definitionFit: The same plural names melancholy traditional music and Oxbridge sporting representatives.

clue.text: Get across for the finest journey

parts.note: the finest is the best
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: An invitation to travel somewhere in style.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something is to have a leg on either side, getting across it.

clue.text: Being obsolete, USS Lee's scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A warship named Lee is out of date and sent to the breakers.
explanation.walkthrough: USS is the prefix for a US Navy ship; 'scrapped' rearranges USS and LEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is of no further value or service.

clue.text: Spot suitable for plants?

definitions.meaning: to spot is to stain or dirty
earth is the stuff plants grow in

explanation.surface: Asking whether a particular place would be good for gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirty something, and the earth in which plants are grown.

clue.text: Out-of-this-world saloon used by typists?

parts.note: outer space lies beyond our world
a saloon is a bar

explanation.surface: A bar on another planet that happens to be frequented by office typists.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key at the bottom of a keyboard that typists press between words.

clue.text: Over-refined quality has pinkies' centres crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone affected crooks the little finger when drinking tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the raised little finger of a fussy tea drinker; 'crooked' rearranges PINKIES and CENTRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive fussiness about small details is an over-refined trait.

clue.text: Many request the small barrel

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Lots of people want the little barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a wooden container for liquids, a small barrel.

clue.text: Light yellow with a look of a bison

parts.note: buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A pale animal with a particular appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the bison is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: They are played out on the boards

definitions.text: They are played out on the boards

parts.words: They are played out on the boards
parts.note: 'the boards' means the stage, and actors play parts there, not games on boards

explanation.surface: Games being played on boards.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts in a play are acted out by performers on stage.

clue.text: Author of play all set to go off — but still it goes on!

definitions.text: Author of play all set to go off — but still it goes on!

parts.words: Author of play all set to go off — but still it goes on!
parts.note: the play is a murder mystery about a trap set to go off, which has run in London since 1952

explanation.surface: A playwright whose show keeps threatening to end but never does.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap, a trap 'set to go off', is the world's longest-running play, still on in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime novelist wrote The Mousetrap, the record-breaking London stage play.

clue.text: Sportingly selecting those who serve best?

definitions.text: Sportingly selecting those who serve best?

parts.words: Sportingly selecting those who serve best?
parts.note: in tennis the top players, who serve well, are ranked and kept apart in the draw

explanation.surface: Picking out the best servants, in a sporting way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' suggests waiting on people; in tennis it is the stroke, and the strongest players are ranked for the draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranking top competitors in a tournament draw so they do not meet early.

clue.text: Like an underwriter's life? Lots of chances in it

definitions.text: Like an underwriter's life? Lots of chances in it

parts.words: Like an underwriter's life? Lots of chances in it
parts.note: an insurance underwriter's job is full of hazards taken on, read as a word meaning full of hazard

explanation.surface: An insurance underwriter's career involves much gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazardous, full of dangers and chances taken.

clue.text: Free — wheeling submarine chain

indicators.note: wheeling means turning round, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A free submarine circles a chain of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock or coral just under the sea's surface.

clue.text: Room high up in backward Italian city

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the Italian word from right to left

parts.note: citta is the Italian word for city

explanation.surface: A high room found in a sleepy old city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian city' is not a named city but the Italian word for one, citta, turned around by 'backward'.
explanation.definitionFit: A space just under a house's roof, the highest room.

clue.text: Ineffective strikes providing clues for CID

definitions.meaning: in British slang fingerprints; CID is the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Weak industrial action that helps detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Light touches, and British slang for fingerprints left as police evidence.

clue.text: Welshman seen in unseemly, notorious places

indicators.note: seen in says the name is visible inside the following words

explanation.surface: A man from Wales spotted in disreputable haunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh boy's name, as in the actor Emlyn Williams.

clue.text: Extreme state

explanation.surface: A country taken to the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete or absolute, and to voice or declare something.

clue.text: Drake's ambition, curiously, was going ashore

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so these letters are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake's goal was strangely to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off a ship onto land.

clue.text: This year revealed wild emotionalism

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A year in which unrestrained feelings were displayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A frenzied state of uncontrolled emotion.

clue.text: One who named the keeper man-of-the-match?

definitions.text: One who named the keeper man-of-the-match?

parts.words: One who named the keeper man-of-the-match?
parts.note: the keeper is not a goalkeeper but D. H. Lawrence's gamekeeper, chosen as her match, i.e. her lover

explanation.surface: Someone choosing the goalkeeper as the best player of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In D. H. Lawrence's novel the heroine takes Mellors the gamekeeper as her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The aristocratic heroine of Lawrence's novel who loves her husband's gamekeeper.

clue.text: Said to be the first floodlight?

indicators.note: said to be tells us the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: the first light at the Flood would be Noah's ark lamp

explanation.surface: Something claimed as the original stadium light.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah's ark rode out the Flood, so an 'ark lamp' would be the first light of the flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful electric light using an arc, used for floodlighting.

clue.text: Pot-bound quadriller?

parts.note: a dancer of the quadrille in Alice in Wonderland who ends up caught in a pot, not a potted plant

explanation.surface: A plant grown too big for its pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot-bound' is a gardening word, but here the pot is a trap; Lewis Carroll wrote of a quadrille danced by these sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish caught in pots and dancing the quadrille in Lewis Carroll's Alice.

clue.text: Imitation scoff

explanation.surface: A fake sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake or sham, and to jeer at someone.

clue.text: Ruler of contrary maids

indicators.note: contrary means perverse or awkward, so the letters are set in a different order

explanation.surface: A king who rules over wayward servants.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary king of Phrygia whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Devil of a discovery about energy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a find is a discovery
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A terrifically difficult finding concerning energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit or demon.

clue.text: Help a felon having article at stake

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a stake is a bet

explanation.surface: Assisting a criminal while gambling on an item.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist or encourage someone in a crime.

clue.text: Did he play maestoso, con fuoco…

definitions.text: Did he play maestoso, con fuoco…

parts.words: Did he play maestoso, con fuoco…
parts.note: con fuoco means with fire; this emperor fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A question about how a musician performed: majestically and with fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Maestoso and con fuoco are musical directions, 'majestically' and 'with fire'; the Roman emperor is said to have fiddled while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor said to have played music as Rome burned.

clue.text: … without feeling?

parts.note: continuing the previous clue, playing without feeling means having no sensation

explanation.surface: Asking whether the musician played without expression.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue's musician, but here 'without feeling' means lacking physical sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking physical sensation, as with cold fingers.

clue.text: Anything costs less than this, love

definitions.meaning: the most expensive thing costs more than anything else
a term of endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Love is priceless, worth more than anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Most costly, and an affectionate term of address for a loved one.

clue.text: Constitutional nature's changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A political constitution's character has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks like an adjective about government; as a noun it is a gentle walk taken for health.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely stroll, like a health walk.

clue.text: Carried off by tube?

parts.note: taken away by underground train, or drawn off liquid through a pipe

explanation.surface: Someone taken away on the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid drawn out through a bent pipe.

clue.text: Housemaid's knee? Perhaps a rub's the answer!

indicators.note: perhaps says this is one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A rub might cure a sore knee from kneeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Housemaid's knee is inflammation of the fluid sac in front of the kneecap, an example of that sac, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluid-filled sac cushioning a joint, as in the knee.
